transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. I'm Ruben. I, uh... I came in because most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling right in my chest. It's like... well, it feels like the old Ruben who could talk to anybody and actually enjoy his day is just gone.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling this way in the past, or is this the first time you've felt like this?

No, I... I don't think I've ever felt quite like this before. I mean, sure, I've had stressful weeks or a bad month here and there. Working in sales, you get used to the ups and downs of the job. But this is different. This is the first time it's been like this, where that heavy feeling just doesn't go away.
How long has this heavy, hollow feeling been present for you?

It's been... about eight months now. It started right around the time we got a new regional manager at work. He just started coming down on me, taking away accounts I'd handled for years. That's when this whole heavy feeling really settled in.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your ability to get a restful night's sleep since this feeling started?

My sleep has definitely changed. At night, I just lie there staring at the ceiling, replaying work stuff over and over in my head. And when I actually do manage to fall asleep, I end up waking up around three or four in the morning. I wake up already worn out, just... dreading the rest of the day.
Have you ever felt so overwhelmed by these feelings that you've had thoughts that life is no longer worth living?

Yes... I have. It's hard to admit, but lately, I've been having these thoughts that... well, that maybe my wife and kids would just be better off if I didn't wake up at all. It's getting to the point where those thoughts really scare me. I just... I don't trust myself the way I used to.
Ruben, when you are feeling this way, have you ever heard voices or seen things that others don't seem to hear or see, or have you had any thoughts that just don't seem based in reality?
No, nothing like that. I haven't heard any voices or seen anything that isn't there. It's just... it's just my own thoughts getting the better of me. But my mind isn't playing tricks on me like that.
Ruben, have you noticed if you feel physically slowed down, like your movements or speech are heavy, or conversely, do you feel restless and unable to sit still?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't feel restless, and I don't think I'm moving or talking any slower than usual. I just feel exhausted all the time, but physically, my movements seem normal.

Ruben, looking back at your life before this eight-month period, can you recall any other time in the past—perhaps years ago—where you felt this same level of deep sadness or loss of interest for at least two weeks?

No, I haven't. I mean, sure, I've had stressful weeks with work or bad days here and there over the years, but... nothing like this. I've never felt this kind of deep sadness before, definitely not for weeks on end. Before this whole thing started eight months ago, I was always pretty steady. So, no, this is the first time it's ever been like this.
Ruben, have you found that you've lost interest or pleasure in the hobbies or activities you used to enjoy before this started?

Yeah, I have. I used to really look forward to things... like bowling, or working out in the garden. Taking my wife to gallery shows, going dancing, things like that. But now... I just sit there. I make excuses not to go out, because none of it feels worth the effort anymore. I just don't have any interest.

Ruben, even if your movements don't look different to others, do you feel a persistent, heavy sense of physical lethargy or 'sluggishness' in your body that makes simple tasks feel like a major effort?

No, not really. I don't feel like my body is physically heavy or anything like that. Like I said before, I'm just exhausted all the time, but it's not a physical weight or a sluggish feeling in my muscles. When I actually get up to do a task, my body works fine... it's just finding the energy or the drive to actually care enough to do it that's the hard part. So, no, I wouldn't say my body feels heavy.
Ruben, have you noticed any difficulty with your ability to focus or concentrate, or have you found it harder than usual to make simple decisions?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My focus seems fine, and I can still make decisions when I need to. It's just... well, like I said, it's more about not having the interest to do things, rather than not being able to concentrate on them. So, no, my concentration and decision-making are about the same as they've always been.
Ruben, do you find yourself feeling a sense of worthlessness or excessive guilt about things that have happened in your life?

Yeah, I do. I just... I keep telling myself I’m completely useless now. I've spent all these years taking care of my clients and providing for my family, doing what I was supposed to do. But lately, it feels like none of that even counts anymore, just because I can’t even handle this job right now. So yeah, I definitely feel a lot of worthlessness.
